newsitem.title: FRANCE: Maize harvest gets under way in France's southwest.
newsitem.headline: Maize harvest gets under way in France's southwest.

text.p: First maize cuttings started last week in France's southwest as crop analysts predicted a sharp rise in yields for the top two producing regions, Aquitaine and Midi-Pyrenees.
But cool temperatures and scattered rain may slow down the maturing and drying process for the grain, they cautioned.
"The crop potential is excellent. But sunny conditions are needed over the next two weeks for the grain to fully dry out," an analyst for the ONIC grain office in Bordeaux told Reuters.
Combining of early variety maize started last week on a few patches in the Hautes-Landes region but harvesting traditionally only gets into full swing in October in France's southwest.
Initial data suggest non-irrigated maize may fare better this year than irrigated maize.
"Irrigated maize yields should be good but not excellent while those of non-irrigated maize should be very good," an analyst for the local ONIC grain ofice in Toulouse said.
Crop analysts explained that while irrigated maize development was somewhat hampered by cool temperatures and rain in August, non-irrigated maize benefited from good moisture levels.
In the Aquitaine region, France's number one maize producer, area is seen up 4.2 percent at 370,000 hectares and yields at the 1993 record of 8.6 tonnes per hectare after 8.0 tonnes last year.
In the Midi-Pyrenees region local ONIC officials put up 4.6 percent at 225,000 hectares. The regional yield is seen rising to around the 1993 record of 7.8 tonnes from 7.2 last year.
The estimate takes into account yields for irrigated maize of 9.0-10 tonnes per hectare and yields for non-irrigated maize of 7.0-7.5 tonnes.
Last week the French maize growers association AGPM predicted the national maize crop may rise by one million tonnes to 13.8 million tonnes in 1996.
The estimate assumes a national yield of 8.0 tonnes per hectare against 7.7 tonnes last year and area of 1.734 million hectares against 1.656 million in 1995.

In a draft prepared ahead of the release of its monthly supply/demand report on September 11, France's grain office ONIC forecast French maize exports to non-EU countries may jump to between 400,000 tonnes and 1.4 million tonnes in the new 1996/97 season (July/June) from just 164,000 tonnes in 1995/96. --Dominique Vidalon, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
